profile.summary: gLM2 is a genomic language model that reads a stretch of genome as a mixture of two alphabets: protein coding regions as amino acids, and the intergenic sequence between them as nucleotides. Each element is prefixed with a strand token. It is a transformer encoder trained by masked language modelling on the OMG metagenomic corpus, and the authors say its representations carry functional information as well as coevolutionary signals in protein-protein interfaces and genomic regulatory syntax.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: Model Description; model card: Model Description; Europe PMC abstract

summary_quotes.text: gLM2 is a mixed-modality genomic language model
It encodes a genomic contig as a sequence of protein coding sequences (CDS) and DNA inter-genic sequences (IGS).
CDS elements are tokenized using per-amino acid tokens, and IGS elements are tokenized using per-nucleotide tokens.
we prepended each genomic element with a special token, either `<+>` or `<->` to indicate the positive and negative strands
that leverages genomic context information to learn robust functional representations, as well as coevolutionary signals in protein-protein interfaces and genomic regulatory syntax

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: gLM2 is a transformer encoder trained with the masked language modelling objective. The input is a contig written as alternating coding and intergenic elements: coding elements as uppercase amino acids, intergenic elements as lowercase nucleotides, so the two alphabets cannot collide, and each element prefixed by <+> or <-> for the strand. The 650M checkpoint's config gives depth 33, dimension 1280, 20 heads, a SwiGLU feed-forward and a vocabulary of 37 tokens; the 150M checkpoint's config gives depth 30, dimension 640 and 10 heads. Pretraining used 315B tokens with a context length of 4096. An update in September 2024 raised the context from 2048 to 4096 tokens and changed intergenic tokenisation from BPE to per-nucleotide.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two checkpoints are published: tattabio/gLM2_150M and tattabio/gLM2_650M. Both cards carry the same September 2024 update note, the same 315B pretraining tokens and the same 4096 context length, and their configs differ in size: depth 33 and dimension 1280 for 650M, depth 30 and dimension 640 for 150M. A result should name which checkpoint was used and its Hugging Face revision, because the September 2024 update changed both the context length and the intergenic tokenisation. This page read the 650M checkpoint at revision 3c4037ae and the 150M checkpoint at revision 93c88529.

limitations.text: Input must be prepared, not raw DNA: coding regions have to be called and translated to uppercase amino acids, intergenic sequence kept as lowercase nucleotides, and each element given a strand token. The tokenizer depends on that case and on the strand tokens.

quotes.text: To avoid collision between amino acid and nucleotide tokens, the tokenizer expects all amino acids to be uppercase, and all nucleotides to be lowercase.
# NOTE: Nucleotides should always be lowercase, and prepended with `<+>`.

limitations.text: The context is 4096 tokens, so only a short stretch of a genome fits in one pass.
The September 2024 update changed the context length and the intergenic tokenisation, so the checkpoint revision matters when reporting a result.

run_guide.summary: Load the gLM2 650M checkpoint and extract embeddings for a short mixed-modality contig.
prerequisites: A CUDA GPU: the published example calls .cuda() and loads the weights in bfloat16. Memory needs are not stated in the sources read.
Code and weights are Apache-2.0 and the checkpoints are not gated.
The input must already be split into coding and intergenic elements, with amino acids uppercase and nucleotides lowercase.

steps.title: Install PyTorch and transformers
steps.explanation: The sources name no install command; this line installs the two packages their usage example imports.

steps.title: Extract embeddings for a contig
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('tattabio/gLM2_650M', torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, trust_remote_code=True).cuda()
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('tattabio/gLM2_650M', trust_remote_code=True)

# A contig with two proteins and an inter-genic sequence.
# NOTE: Nucleotides should always be lowercase, and prepended with `<+>`.
sequence = "<+>MALTKVEKRNRIKRRVRGKISGTQASPRLSVYKSNK<+>aatttaaggaa<->MLGIDNIERVKPGGLELVDRLVAVNRVTKVTKGGRAFGFSAIVVVGNED"

# Tokenize the sequence.
encodings = tokenizer([sequence], return_tensors='pt')

# Extract embeddings.
with torch.no_grad():
    embeddings = model(encodings.input_ids.cuda(), output_hidden_states=True).last_hidden_state
PY
